News about one of the four major C++ compiler front-ends:

EDG is now open source. Here’s what comes next

by Harry Bott

From the announcement:

The code is available under the Apache 2.0 license with LLVM exceptions. This permissive license allows commercial use, including incorporating EDG into proprietary products, subject to terms. For companies building C++ tools, this provides an ideal option for a front end that adapts to your needs. ...

We're excited about ways the community can make it even better. EDG has experimental support for reflection for C++26, which lets programs inspect information about types and declarations at compile time. ...
